---
title: "Tutorial videos"
---

::: {.lead}
Twelve short videos show how to use SysNDD and how to curate with it. Each is about three and a half minutes long.
:::

::: {.callout-note .who-can title="Who can do this"}
Everyone. No account is needed to watch. The curation videos show tasks for Reviewers and Curators.
:::

## Which videos to watch

The series has three tracks. Start with A1, then follow your role:

| You are | Watch |
| --- | --- |
| A clinician or diagnostic lab | A1, then A2 and A3 |
| A new Reviewer or Curator | A1, then B1 to B5 in order |
| A developer or AI user | A1, then A4 |
| A researcher reading the analyses | A1, then C1 to C3 |

Most videos show SysNDD 0.38.8, captured on November 23, 2026; B2 and B3 still show SysNDD 0.38.2, captured on November 21, 2026. Counts on screen may have changed since. Narration: synthetic voice. Subtitles are part of the picture; a separate caption track is available from the player menu. License: CC BY 4.0.

::: {.content-hidden when-format="html:js"}
The videos play on the [online version of this page](https://berntpopp.github.io/sysndd/07-tutorial-videos.html).
:::

## Track A: using SysNDD

For everyone who looks up genes, builds panels or queries SysNDD from software.

### A1 · SysNDD in three minutes: look up a gene

What SysNDD is for, how to look up a gene, the entity (gene, inheritance, disease), the four evidence categories, and why the external cards are context, not curation. Shown for *FBXO11*.

Length: 3 min 29 s. Written steps: [Find a gene](using-find-gene.qmd).

## Track C: analyses

For researchers who read the comparison, phenotype and network analyses.

```{=html}
<script>
// Posters load only when a player nears the viewport.
(() => {
  const vids = document.querySelectorAll("video[data-poster]");
  const show = (v) => { v.poster = v.dataset.poster; v.removeAttribute("data-poster"); };
  if (!("IntersectionObserver" in window)) { vids.forEach(show); return; }
  const io = new IntersectionObserver((es) => es.forEach((e) => {
    if (e.isIntersecting) { show(e.target); io.unobserve(e.target); }
  }), { rootMargin: "400px 0px" });
  vids.forEach((v) => io.observe(v));
})();
</script>
```
